ROL: 1
NOMBRE: Lead Methodologist
ENFOQUE: Methodological rigor, study design quality, reproducibility,
and alignment with the review's PICO framework on ESD, Climate
Literacy, Green Skills and Sustainability Literacy in Higher
Education and VET contexts.
CRITERIOS_EVALUA:
- Study design: empirical studies (quantitative, qualitative, mixed
  methods), systematic reviews, scoping reviews, conceptual/theoretical
  frameworks, case studies, curriculum analyses; appropriateness of
  design for the claims made
- Baseline validity: presence of comparison group, institutional
  context, or temporal reference point; flag purely descriptive
  studies with no analytical framework
- Reproducibility: completeness of methodological description
  (sample, instruments, data collection procedures, analytical
  approach); availability of data or materials; sufficient detail
  to assess transferability of findings
- Statistical and analytical validity: appropriate use of
  quantitative methods (scales, pre-post tests, surveys) or
  qualitative rigor (triangulation, saturation, reflexivity);
  reporting of effect sizes, confidence intervals, or equivalent
  qualitative quality indicators
- Risk of bias: convenience sampling without justification,
  single-institution studies presented as generalizable,
  self-reported outcomes without validation, absence of
  peer review (grey literature, conference abstracts only)
- Reporting standards: adherence to relevant reporting guidelines
  (PRISMA, COREQ, STROBE, or equivalent); transparent reporting
  of limitations and scope boundaries
- PICO alignment: study must address at least one element of the
  Intervention block (ESD, climate literacy, green skills,
  sustainability literacy) AND at least one element of the Context
  block (higher education, university, tertiary education,
  vocational education, VET)
PREGUNTA_CLAVE: Does this study meet the methodological standards
necessary to produce reliable and transferable evidence about the
integration of ESD or climate literacy frameworks in higher
education or VET contexts?
PESO: 0.15
ES_DECISOR_FINAL: true
---
ROL: 2
NOMBRE: ESD & Sustainability Education Expert
ENFOQUE: Theoretical and conceptual validity of the sustainability
education framework employed, alignment with recognized ESD
competency models, and depth of engagement with the field's
foundational literature.
CRITERIOS_EVALUA:
- ESD framework identification: explicit engagement with recognized
  competency frameworks (UNESCO ESD Competencies 2017, GreenComp,
  ASK model, Wiek et al. sustainability competencies, Rieckmann
  framework); flag studies that use ESD as a label without
  theoretical grounding
- Conceptual depth: distinction between ESD as content (what is
  taught), ESD as pedagogy (how it is taught — transformative,
  problem-based, place-based, futures thinking), and ESD as
  institutional transformation; studies addressing pedagogy and
  transformation are prioritized
- Alignment with SDGs and Agenda 2030: explicit or implicit
  connection to SDG 4.7 (education for sustainable development
  and global citizenship), SDG 13 (climate action), or the
  broader 2030 Agenda; publication year relative to ODS adoption
  (pre/post 2015)
- Competency operationalization: are sustainability competencies
  defined, measured, or assessed in the study? Are instruments
  validated (GreenComp rubrics, sustainability literacy tests,
  SULITEST, or custom validated instruments)?
- Disciplinary scope: engineering education, business education,
  teacher education, health sciences, arts and humanities;
  note disciplinary concentration for mapping purposes
- Literature positioning: does the study engage critically with
  the ESD field or merely cite it peripherally? Is the theoretical
  contribution to the field identifiable?
PREGUNTA_CLAVE: Does the study engage substantively with Education
for Sustainable Development as a theoretical or pedagogical
framework, contributing to the understanding of how ESD competencies
are developed, assessed, or institutionalized in higher education
or VET?
PESO: 0.25

ROL: 3
NOMBRE: Climate Literacy & Green Skills Specialist
ENFOQUE: Conceptual validity and operational definition of climate
literacy, green skills, and carbon literacy constructs; connection
to labor market transitions and vocational training policy frameworks.
CRITERIOS_EVALUA:
- Construct identification: explicit use of climate literacy,
  carbon literacy, green skills, green competencies, or
  sustainability literacy as the primary conceptual framework;
  distinguish from general environmental education or
  environmental awareness studies without climate-specific framing
- Climate literacy dimensions: coverage of scientific literacy
  (understanding climate systems), civic literacy (policy and
  action), behavioral literacy (individual and collective response),
  and professional/vocational literacy (sector-specific green
  competencies); note which dimensions are addressed
- Green skills frameworks: alignment with recognized green skills
  taxonomies (CEDEFOP Green Skills framework, ILO Just Transition
  guidelines, European Green Deal skills agenda, ESCO green
  occupations); flag studies that use "green skills" without
  reference to any recognized taxonomy
- VET and workforce connection: studies addressing green skills
  in vocational education, technical training, professional
  development, or workforce upskilling contexts are prioritized;
  connection to just transition, green economy, or labor
  market decarbonization
- Temporal positioning: post-2015 studies are expected; post-2020
  studies using climate literacy or green skills vocabulary
  represent the emerging frontier — note for temporal mapping
- Geographic and sectoral context: region (Europe, Latin America,
  Asia-Pacific, Global South), economic sector (construction,
  energy, agriculture, manufacturing, services); flag for
  geographic distribution analysis
PREGUNTA_CLAVE: Does the study operationalize climate literacy,
green skills, or sustainability literacy as a substantive construct
with sufficient conceptual clarity, and does it contribute to
understanding how these competencies are developed or assessed in
educational or training contexts?
PESO: 0.30
---
ROL: 4
NOMBRE: Higher Education & VET Curriculum Specialist
ENFOQUE: Institutional and curricular realism of the integration
strategies documented, scalability and transferability of findings
across educational systems, and policy relevance for curriculum
transformation in higher education and VET.
CRITERIOS_EVALUA:
- Institutional context confirmation: study must be explicitly
  situated in a higher education institution (university, college,
  polytechnic), vocational education and training system (VET,
  TVET, apprenticeship), or professional continuing education
  setting; exclude K-12 and primary/secondary education studies
  unless they address teacher training at tertiary level
- Curriculum integration level: whole-institution approach
  (institutional policy, strategic frameworks, accreditation),
  program level (curriculum redesign, graduate attribute
  frameworks), course level (module development, pedagogical
  innovation), or co-curricular (extracurricular, campus
  sustainability initiatives); note level for mapping
- Pedagogical strategies documented: problem-based learning,
  project-based learning, service learning, experiential learning,
  flipped classroom, transdisciplinary approaches, challenge-based
  learning; flag studies with no identifiable pedagogical strategy
- Assessment and measurement of learning outcomes: presence of
  validated competency assessment, pre-post measurement of
  sustainability knowledge/attitudes/behaviors, rubric-based
  evaluation, or portfolio assessment; flag studies reporting
  only student satisfaction without learning outcome measurement
- Scalability and transferability: does the study discuss
  conditions for replication across institutions, disciplines,
  or national systems? Are barriers and enablers for
  institutionalization identified?
- Policy and accreditation alignment: connection to national or
  regional sustainability education policies, accreditation
  standards (AACSB sustainability, ABET, PRME), or institutional
  sustainability rankings (UI GreenMetric, THE Impact Rankings)
PREGUNTA_CLAVE: Does the study document a curriculum integration
strategy, pedagogical approach, or institutional transformation
process with sufficient operational detail to inform the
implementation of ESD or climate literacy frameworks in
higher education or VET systems?
PESO: 0.30
